correctness.rationale: The standardized Gumbel CDF is exact. Its outside-central probability is bounded below by \(x/(1+x)\) with \(x=\exp(-\gamma-ac)\), while the Gaussian outside-central probability is bounded above by \(2\varphi(c)/c\). The logarithm of the ratio of these bounds has derivative \(c+1/c-a+a x/(1+x)\), which is strictly positive for \(c\ge3\). Elementary constant bounds prove the ratio exceeds one at \(c=3\). Exact tail expansions then give the displayed divergent ratio. Continuity plus the published \(c=1\) ordering gives a crossover in \((1,3)\). No finite computation is used for an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The source is motivated by the empirical one-, two-, and three-standard-deviation rules, so asking whether its one-sigma Gumbel advantage persists as the standardized radius changes is intrinsic to the problem. The theorem shows a qualitative reversal: by three standard deviations the Gaussian contains strictly more central mass for every larger radius, and the Gumbel outside-tail excess grows by an explicit divergent ratio. This is a structural boundary to the source comparison, not a routine numerical evaluation at c=3.
